FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.98  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.94  
DESCRIPTION: The highest-severity missed defect is upstream of the immune code: Experiment 17 feeds `DynamicManager.process_round()` a fabricated one-entry response map keyed as `"combined"` instead of the real per-model responses in [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L853), [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L866), and [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L898). But `process_round()` treats `responses` as the authoritative per-model input for failure handling, per-model cost allocation, and immune model tracking in [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5045), [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5119), and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5153). That makes every real model look absent, injects a bogus out-of-pool `"combined"` responder, and invalidates the experiment’s immune/load-balancing telemetry. `_build_model_responses()` also hardcodes `response_time=0.0` and `format_compliant=True` in [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1364) and [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1366), so even a partial fix would still feed falsified metadata.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Preserve and pass the real per-model `ModelResponse` objects produced during dispatch; reject synthetic response keys not in the manager pool; assert that `finding.model_id` is a subset of the expected responder set for the round; and carry through real latency/format/decomposition metadata rather than rebuilding placeholder responses.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.89  
DESCRIPTION: The dispatch false-positive interface is too weak to represent the event it claims to detect. `check_dispatch_health()` only receives round-number lists and diagnoses when a success round is strictly later than a block round (`s > block_round`) in [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4087). But the Experiment 17 runner auto-decomposes immediately after a block in the same round in [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1260), and the feasibility gate is explicitly applied even to already-decomposed prompts in [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1254). So the current API cannot distinguish the intended pathology “full prompt blocked, decomposed retry succeeded” from “already-decomposed prompt blocked,” and it structurally misses same-round rescues even if success recording is added.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the round-only `dispatch_blocks` / `dispatch_successes` lists with structured dispatch-attempt records containing at least `round_idx`, `prompt_mode` (`full` or `decomposed`), `blocked`, `retry_of`, and `succeeded`. Diagnose false positives only from matched full-prompt block -> decomposed retry success pairs, including same-round pairs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.87  
DESCRIPTION: Ownership of `pre_decompose_models` is broken. The experiment runner writes directly to `mgr.config.pre_decompose_models` on feasibility block and throughput fallback in [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1268) and [run_exp17_immune.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1279), while the immune system treats the same state as a managed remediation target and only logs/audits it when it goes through `apply_diagnosis()` and `_record_adjustment()` in [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5714) and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6005). This means identical state changes can happen outside damping, regression snapshots, and immune audit/history. It also conflates different causes: operator policy, throughput workaround, model-failure remediation, and dispatch-false-positive learning all collapse into one bare set, so later code cannot tell why a model is being decomposed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the bare set with a manager-owned structured decomposition policy store keyed by model and cause/source. Expose one API for all decomposition-policy changes, and have both the runner and `apply_diagnosis()` call that API so provenance, damping, regression tracking, and audit logging stay coherent.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Boundary note: the strongest missed defect is not inside `LoadBalancer` itself. It is the upstream Experiment 17 harness feeding invalid inputs into the immune/load-balancing layer, which makes several downstream detector behaviors uninterpretable.
